blind_target.authors: Eikeseth, S., Smith, T., Jahr, E., & Eldevik, S.
blind_target.title: Outcome for children with autism who began intensive behavioral treatment between ages 4 and 7.
blind_target.evidence_quote:
The present study supports previous findings from investigators such as
Eikeseth et al. (2007) that EIBI, using the Lovaas/UCLA Model, can be
implemented in a nonuniversity setting and that favorable results can be
achieved for children above the age of 3½ years at entry into treatment.
blind_target.outcome_quote:
In addition, given the
wide age range of our sample, the results also support previous findings that
some children who are 4 to 6 years old at onset of EIBI can make substantial
gains in IQ, adaptive behavior, and school placement (Eikeseth et al., 2007).
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: The report also re-tests efficacy when intervention begins after early preschool age. It explicitly identifies its results as supporting Eikeseth et al. (2007) for substantial gains among children starting at ages 4–6. The 2007 outcome report is the closest cited target for this longer-term finding; the 2002 interim report is not separately targeted.

luna_triage.reason: The Discussion explicitly relates the present study’s results to Eikeseth et al. (2007): it reports greater improvement for EIBI than services as usual across outcome measures, and says results support findings for children starting EIBI at ages 4–6. The reference list identifies the 2007 empirical report. The only supplied shipped row is Cohen et al. (2006), a separate community-setting study and not the Eikeseth age-at-onset report.
